section_locator: Full article read. Definitions and implicit-definability/invariance: pp. 359-362. Worldline becoming, worldline transitivity, meshing and Lemma: pp. 362-364. relevance: Primary predecessor establishing a classification of absolute and worldline-dependent objective-becoming relations under explicit adequacy assumptions in time-oriented Minkowski spacetime. It substantially pre-empts a broad novelty claim for such a classification.

assumptions.shared_conventions: The model is 3+1 Minkowski spacetime (R^4, eta) with a chosen objective time orientation T. The authors explicitly take I± and J± reflexively for convenience, including I−; thus I− here is reflexive closure of strict chronological past. For an absolute relation B, objective becoming requires implicit definability from the time-oriented metric (equivalently invariance under all time-orientation-preserving metric automorphisms) and transitivity.
assumptions.theorem_1: Absolute/worldline-independent B additionally satisfies chronological becoming I− ⊆ B. The theorem does not assume causal becoming J− ⊆ B and states no separate non-universality condition.
assumptions.lemma_and_theorem_2: The family {B_λ} ranges over all inextendible timelike worldlines, not a selected actual observer family. Worldline becoming requires the reflexive chronological past of b along λ to be included in B_λ(b). Worldline transitivity quantifies across arbitrary λ and μ: a∈B_λ(b) and b∈B_μ(c) imply a∈B_μ(c). Meshing defines absolute B by agreement of all λ through b. For Theorem 2, each B_λ is implicitly definable from the time-oriented metric plus that corresponding λ, invariant under its λ-preserving automorphisms; no other privileged lines or initial global surface are included.

conclusion: Theorem 1: under implicit time-oriented metric definability, transitivity, and I− ⊆ B, B is exactly I−, J−, or universal U. The Lemma derives I− ⊆ B from worldline becoming plus cross-worldline transitivity and meshing; it does not derive null-cone inclusion. Theorem 2: under worldline becoming, cross-worldline transitivity, and each-line implicit definability from the time-oriented metric plus that line, uniformly every B_λ is the restriction of I−, or uniformly every B_λ is the restriction of J−, or uniformly every B_λ is the restriction of U. Distinguished sets of worldlines/initial surfaces fall outside the theorem’s stated structure. The article does not establish an ontology from SR or advocate objective becoming.
